answer: The network can price new identities with a dynamic registration vault: the stake required to mint an identity rises automatically when many registrations arrive from correlated sources in one epoch, like a jade market that charges more as demand crowds in. The stake sits in a shared vault and is returned only after three clean epochs, so a sybil farmer pays an inflated, marble-hard price per fake exactly when it tries to mint in bulk. One honest agent registers once at the base price, while a thousand fakes face a price curve that climbs with every additional key.
